entries.question: Which referencing style should I use?
variants: What is the referencing style used at NCI?
how do I cite sources in my assignment
entries.answer: NCI uses three referencing styles. Harvard is the most widely used, across most School of Business courses and some School of Computing modules. APA is used by Psychology, Education and Learning and Teaching students. IEEE is used in some School of Computing modules. Harvard is an author-date system: you put a short (Author, Year) citation in the text and a full reference in a list titled References, in alphabetical order by author surname and with no numbering. Every in-text citation must match a reference list entry and vice versa. Always confirm the exact style your module requires with your lecturer.

entries.question: How do I apply for an assignment extension?
variants: how do I get more time for my assignment

entries.answer: Extensions are only considered in exceptional circumstances and you must provide evidence. Submit the request through NCI360, and allow for the standard 7 working days, or up to 14 where there is good reason. Send the request at least 5 days before the original submission deadline, because an extension cannot be granted retrospectively. Approvals are recorded in your assessment plan, and you should get written confirmation before you assume the new date applies.

entries.question: How do I resit an exam?
variants: how do I repeat an exam
what happens if I fail an exam
entries.answer: For an in-class assessment, you apply for a resit within 5 days of the original scheduled date. If it is granted, the resit is scheduled during class time in the final week of the semester, which NCI calls Assessment Contingency Week, and there is only one resit opportunity per in-class assessment. Routine workload, poor time management and technical problems are not valid grounds unless the problem was independently verified at the time. This policy does not cover end-of-semester exams, which are handled under the College's assessment deferral policy.

entries.question: How do I submit my assignment on Moodle?
entries.answer: Open your module page in Moodle, go to the assessment you are submitting, click the submission link and upload your file. If the upload fails, take a screenshot and contact the module lecturer or Student Services the same day. I cannot see the per-module upload link, so please use the one in your Moodle module page.

entries.question: How do I register for my seat for the new year?

entries.answer: Online registration for returning full-time and part-time students opens in July 2026. If you are not in receipt of a SUSI grant you must pay at least 20% of the Student Contribution Fee to register, plus the 80 euro gym fee. entries.question: Are there scholarships or financial support available?
entries.answer: Yes. NCI runs a range of scholarships, grants and discounts, and the live list with deadlines and how to apply is on the Scholarships and Discounts page. The postgraduate schemes for September 2026 entry included the Master's Edge Scholarship, which is 25% off a full-time, day-time Masters or Postgraduate Diploma for qualified NCI students and alumni; a full Irish Refugee Council postgraduate scholarship for one candidate; the 30% Club scholarship, which gives two fully funded places, one in the School of Business and Social Sciences and one in the School of Computing; and a 1,000 euro discount for NCI students and alumni. Those deadlines were in May, June and August 2026 and have now passed, so treat them as the pattern rather than as an open application, and check the page for the current round. Note that scholarships cannot be combined, so only the scholarship of highest value is awarded, and that the Master's Edge is daytime only while the 30% Club covers full-time and part-time study. Many of these are not available to students paying international fees, who have a separate scholarship portfolio. Separately from scholarships, if you are in receipt of a SUSI grant you may qualify for the Free Fees Initiative. If money is the barrier to you studying, talk to Student Services about the Student Assistance Fund, the Fund for Students with Disabilities, the emergency hardship fund for international students, and the option of paying by direct debit.

entries.question: What internship or placement opportunities are there?
variants: how do I find an internship
entries.answer: Some MSc programmes include a work placement as a graded part of the degree. The School of Computing placement programmes run for 12 weeks, either May to August or September to December, and include MSc in Cybersecurity, MSc in Artificial Intelligence, MSc in AI for Business, MSc in Data Analytics and MSc in FinTech. On these placements students typically work four days a week in the company and attend class at NCI on the fifth day, so confirm your own pattern with the Careers Team. Whether a placement is a formal credit-bearing part of your programme or something you arrange yourself depends on your course, so check the Courses with Work Placement page for your programme or ask your programme co-ordinator. Independently of that, the NCI online jobs board is updated daily with jobs and placements employers have sent in, and it is accessed from MyApps using your NCI login. entries.question: How do I reset my NCI password?
entries.answer: Go to https://password.ncirl.ie/ and choose the option that fits: Sign up for SSPR to register self-service password reset, Reset Password if you have forgotten it, or Change Password if you know your current one. This is the same password you use for Moodle, MyDetails, Office 365 and Wi-Fi, so resetting it updates everything at once. If you enter it incorrectly several times your IT account is locked, and the Password Management service is also what unlocks it. If you cannot recover it yourself, raise a ticket with IT through the NCI Support Hub at https://ncisupporthub.ncirl.ie/hc/en-ie .

entries.question: How do I connect to NCI Wi-Fi?
entries.answer: Select the network named eduroam on your device and sign in with your NCI credentials: username x12345678@student.ncirl.ie and your NCI password. eduroam is the international research and education roaming network, so the same username and password also work at thousands of other participating universities worldwide, which is useful if you are travelling. On Android 8 or later and on iPhone, the easiest method is to install the free geteduroam app, search for National College of Ireland, choose National College of Ireland IE, then log in and select Join. On Windows set security to WPA2 Enterprise, authentication to PEAP, and the domain to ncirl.ie. If it fails, forget the network on your device to clear any cached password, reset your password, and contact itupport@ncirl.ie if it still will not connect.

entries.question: How do I book a library study room?

entries.answer: There are 8 study rooms bookable in the library, plus 2 more on the 1st floor of the Spencer Dock building (S1.12 for 6 people and S1.13 for 8). You must be on Eduroam Wi-Fi to check in, and you should check out if you leave early. entries.question: What are the requirements for my MSc dissertation?
variants: when do I submit my dissertation
entries.answer: The dissertation is independent research of your own topic, and the exact requirements are set by your programme's handbook, not by the college as a whole. The minimum requirements for a Level 9 dissertation are published in the Dissertation Submission Specifications and the School of Business Postgraduate Dissertation Handbook, both linked from the library's Thesis and Final Year Project Submission Guide. In summary you submit electronically through Moodle (Turnitin), a hard copy is no longer required, you must complete and sign the Submission of Thesis and Declaration form and attach it, you must turn off any file security before uploading, and an approved electronic copy is then deposited in the library repository NORMA. You are allocated a supervisor. Some programmes set the dissertation due date in August after the taught modules finish, so check your programme handbook and your module page in Moodle. Turnitin also generates the report for checking similarity and AI use, so submit well before the deadline and do not leave generating the report to the last minute.

entries.question: What happens if I submit my assignment late?
entries.answer: Late coursework is penalised at 5% of the awarded mark for each calendar day it is late, up to a maximum deduction of 100%. The penalty applies only to the specific item that is late, not to your overall module grade. Nothing is accepted after the date of the relevant Examination Board, and work submitted after that date is treated as a non-submission and given a mark of zero. If you already have an approved extension, the penalty runs from the expiry of the extended deadline. To appeal, contact the Office of the Registrar at registrarsoffice@ncirl.ie.

entries.question: Can I defer an exam?
entries.answer: Yes. You can request a deferral for your full programme, for a single module, or for a single assessment, and for a repeat assessment, by submitting the request through NCI360. There are no fees for a deferral request. The Exams Team handles the request and will confirm the outcome, so if you have not heard back, or you need to discuss your circumstances, email exams@ncirl.ie. A deferred assessment is rescheduled to the next sitting of that assessment. If you are an international student, tell the International Office as well, because a change to your completion date can affect your visa renewal.

entries.question: What happens if I fail a module, and can I repeat it?
entries.answer: If you fail a module at your first attempt you can repeat that assessment or exam at the next repeat sitting, which is called repeat by assessment. You do not have to retake the whole course. September starters sit repeat exams in August. If you fail both at your first attempt and at the resit, you have to repeat by attending classes the following academic year. If the module counts towards your final award, your grade for it is capped at a Pass, 40%, after a repeat, but this capped grade does not limit your overall award classification. Repeats are not free: there is a registration fee plus a fee per module. You also cannot repeat a module you have already passed just to get a better mark.

entries.question: How do I contact Academic Operations?
entries.answer: Academic Operations runs the Support Hub on the ground floor of the Mayor Square building. Online support is available from 8am to 6:30pm Monday to Thursday and 8am to 5pm on Friday. Walk-in appointments run 9am to 4pm Monday to Friday. They handle assessment records, deferrals and deferral requests, repeat registration, exam results queries, graduation and confirmation letters, and changes to your registration such as adding or dropping a module.

entries.question: What is the NCI Support Hub?
entries.answer: The Support Hub is NCI's main student services point, on the ground floor of the Mayor Square building. It is the first place to go for anything you are not sure about, and staff can point you to the right team rather than leaving you to guess. The NCI Library, Academic Operations and IT support all sit within or alongside it. If you have a question that is not in this assistant, this is the right place to get an authoritative answer.

entries.question: What are the main student systems and how do I log in?
entries.answer: All of your main systems use the same NCI student email address and password, in the form x12345678@student.ncirl.ie. Moodle is at moodle2026.ncirl.ie and holds your course pages, lecture material, assignment submissions and your timetable. MyApps is the Microsoft 365 portal for free Office, Teams and the software catalogue. NCI360 is where you make official requests, including extensions, deferrals and repeats. MyDetails is where your personal details, fees and enrolment are held. The Support Hub knowledge base is at ncisupporthub.ncirl.ie. If you are locked out of any of them, reset your password first, then contact IT support if it still fails.

entries.question: Where can I get help if I am struggling?
entries.answer: If you are feeling overwhelmed, anxious or low, please talk to someone. NCI's Student Counselling and Wellness Service is the right first step, and you can book an appointment directly through their page. They also support issues such as eating disorders, addiction or substance use, confidence and self-esteem, and LGBTQIA+ support. You can also see your programme co-ordinator or the Students' Union, and NCI's Student Support Services FAQ covers the practical side. If something is affecting your studies, tell someone early, because support is much easier to arrange before a deadline. In an emergency, or if you or someone else is in immediate danger, contact emergency services.
